football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Miami, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.7 of the 5.3 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.

When Florida State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Florida State’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.2% of its dropbacks, and Miami’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Florida State has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Florida State’s offense averages 5.3 yards per carry, and Miami’s defense allows 2.8 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).
contradicting: When Miami has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Miami’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.2% of its dropbacks, and Florida State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
